title: Confronting a Colleague Who Took Credit in the Room
script: Melati: [controlled] Arman, I want to talk about the client meeting, specifically the moment you presented the retention strategy as though it hadn't originated entirely from my proposal.
Arman: [defensive] That's a fairly uncharitable reading. I presented the strategy the team had landed on, which happens to include work from several of us.
Melati: [firm] The team landed on it after I'd already written the document, line by line, at eleven o'clock on a Sunday you weren't copied on.
Arman: [uncomfortable] I didn't intend to erase your contribution, if that's how it registered. These presentations move quickly, and attribution isn't always foremost in my mind under pressure.
Melati: [pointed] Attribution rarely is foremost in the mind of whoever benefits from its absence, which is precisely why it requires deliberate effort rather than passive good intentions.
Arman: [conceding] That lands harder than I'd like to admit, mostly because I suspect it's accurate.
Melati: [measured] I'm not interested in a lengthy confession. I'm interested in what changes the next time we're both in a room with people whose opinions actually shape our trajectories.
Arman: [thoughtful] What would that look like, concretely, rather than as a vague promise I make and quietly forget by Thursday?
Melati: [direct] Name me explicitly when the idea is mine. It costs you nothing measurable and costs me considerably, compounding, when you don't.
Arman: [honest] I think part of what happened is that crediting you felt, unconsciously, like diminishing my own visibility in a room I was nervous about impressing.
Melati: [understanding] That's a more honest explanation than most people manage, though I'd point out that visibility built on someone else's uncredited labour is a fairly unstable foundation.
Arman: [reflective] Put that plainly, I can't really defend it. I think I've been treating credit as a fixed pie, when it clearly isn't, or doesn't have to be.
Melati: [warmly] It isn't, generally, provided the people distributing it are actually paying attention rather than defaulting to whoever spoke last and loudest.
Arman: [determined] Understood. Next meeting, I name you first, explicitly, before I say anything else about the strategy at all.
Melati: [genuine] That's all I was asking for, Arman. Not an apology tour, just the accuracy the work actually earned.

quiz.question: What specifically does Melati confront Arman about?
options: Missing a deadline
Presenting her retention strategy without acknowledging it originated from her proposal
Being late to the client meeting
Disagreeing with her in front of the client
quiz.explanation: Melati confronts Arman for presenting her retention strategy as a team effort without crediting its actual origin.

quiz.question: What excuse does Arman initially offer?
options: He forgot she existed
Presentations move quickly and attribution isn't always foremost in his mind under pressure
He didn't know she wrote it
He thought she wanted anonymity
quiz.explanation: Arman initially claims attribution isn't foremost in his mind during fast-moving presentations under pressure.

quiz.question: What does Melati say about attribution and who benefits from its absence?
options: Attribution is unimportant in professional settings
Attribution rarely is foremost in the mind of whoever benefits from its absence, requiring deliberate effort
Attribution should never be discussed openly
Attribution only matters for junior employees
quiz.explanation: Melati points out that attribution conveniently isn't top of mind for whoever benefits from its absence, requiring deliberate effort instead.

quiz.question: What honest explanation does Arman eventually offer for his behavior?
options: He genuinely disliked Melati
Crediting her felt, unconsciously, like diminishing his own visibility in a room he was nervous about impressing
He was told to do it by his manager
He had no explanation at all
quiz.explanation: Arman admits crediting Melati unconsciously felt like it would diminish his own visibility while nervous about impressing the room.

quiz.question: What specific change does Arman commit to?
options: Never speaking in meetings again
Naming Melati first, explicitly, before saying anything else about the strategy
Quitting the project entirely
Writing her a formal apology letter
quiz.explanation: Arman commits to explicitly naming Melati first in the next meeting before discussing the strategy at all.
